newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse firm on demand for financials.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse firm on demand for financials.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index firmed marginally on Thursday on strong demand for financials fuelled by speculation on anticipated year-end results.
The index went up 2.59 points to close at 3522.86. Turnover eased to 23.535 million shillings on 559,016 shares from 66.426 million shillings on 1,396,366 shares.
"Turnover in the market dropped because there was no activity on the special boards today, but otherwise the volumes traded were still impressive," a bourse official said.
Brokers predicted that focus would be on the financials for at least the next two weeks as they would be announcing their results anytime in February.
The race they said, will be between Kenya Commercial Bank, Standard Chartered Bank and Barclays Bank. Going by history Barclays is normally the first to announce and is considered the market leader.
"But this year will be very interesting to watch. Kenya Commercial Banks market image changed after its third public share offer in October and it has earned a lot of goodwill," a senior broker said.

"We're suspecting that Standard Chartered might issue a bonus since they did not issue one last year. They also underwent a massive restructuring programme so their performance should be better," another broker said.
A financial analyst said the prevailing bullish tone of the market would remain for as long as Kenyan investors had something to look forward to.
Heavy foreign demand has also sustained bull prices on some key shares.

Firestone East Africa traded at 30 from 30.25, while Sasini Tea & Coffee traded at 75 unchanged. Oil concern Total Kenya edged one shilling to close at 94 while British American Tobacco (BAT) Kenya closed at 41 from 40.75.
Power share was stable at 90 unchanged, while Kenya Airways closed at 8.75 from 8.65.
Barclays Bank traded at 113 from 112 while Standard Chartered Bank firmed to 54 from 53.50.
Kenya Commercial Bank closed at 90 from 90.50.
